blocks.content: The principles included in this category represent the ideology of liberalism.

rows: Uniform Civil Code for all citizens
Early childhood care & education up to age 6
Subject matter modified by 86th Amendment Act (2002)
Protection of environment, forests, and wildlife
Separation of judiciary from executive in public service
Promotion of international peace and security
Forms the constitutional basis of India's Foreign Policy

items: Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) is frequently asked in UPSC/State PCS examinations under Indian Polity.
Article 48A was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 to protect environment and wildlife.
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 modified Article 45, shifting primary education to Article 21A as a Fundamental Right.
Article 50 (Separation of Judiciary from Executive) is a frequently asked direct question in prelims.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 44 directs the State to secure for all citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India.
Article 45 mandates early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
Article 48 seeks to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.
Article 48A obligates the State to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife.
Article 50 directs the separation of the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.
Article 51 promotes international peace and security, just relations between nations, and respect for international law.
